protocol.what: A4 re-runs the P0.5 measurement through FoldMatch's production implementation (ESM3 residue path of build/query, the P2 encoder module, the P3 kernel, the P4 statistics) on each device class it claims, and compares with the RESEARCH encodings exactly as P0.5 did.
protocol.inputs_note: sets.json (sha256 above) fixes every id, sequence key (sha1 of the normalised sequence) and order; q200 = 200 benchmark queries stratified by M3 length bin (34/34/33/33/33/33, default_rng(20260927)); tsub = the 789 targets of P_sub

P_sub.definition: research lnE <= 0 (E <= 1): shipped table all, Q90 = bench_q90_shipped.npy (shipped panel), N = annotated residues of the 50,000 benchmark targets; <= 8 hits per query sampled with default_rng(20260928)

protocol.reference: research encodings: queries evalue/encode/out/queries.L2m_B8_s0.npz (md5 e821497f...), targets targets.L2m_B8_s0.npz (cfee06cd...), panel shipped_panel_codes.npz (15cc1c7b...), chains sw_mlp/enc/L2m_B8_s0.chains.npz (55198660...), enc_check sw_mlp/enc_check/L2m_B8_s0.npz; research lnE from the research S_D matrices (evalue/score/out) and bench_q90_shipped.npy (P0.5 recomputation: Q90 identical, P_sub S max |d| 1e-4)

evalue.formula: lnE = lnK(m) + ln m + ln N - lambda(m) (S - Q90); lambda, lnK = np.interp(ln m, ln centre, table) (ship_final 'all'); S = float64(S_f) - float64(S_r), setting D (1.0; 5/0.5), S_r = query rows reversed; Q90 = np.quantile(S(query, 1,000 shipped panel codes), 0.9); m = query length; N = annotated residues of the 50,000 benchmark targets

metrics.code_bits: fraction of equal code bits vs the research codes, POOLED over panel + enccheck + chains + tsub (783,823 residues, 50,164,672 bits)
metrics.dlnE: lnE(config) - lnE(research) on the P_sub pairs; config = (query-encoding device, target-code device); each config's Q90 = its own q vs the SHIPPED research panel codes; |dlnE| median and P95 over the pairs
metrics.dF1: mean SW F1 (setting D, chain_eval.prf vs the US-align primary reference) over the 582 similar chain-set pairs minus the research M8_s0 setting-D value 0.613393 (evalue/f1_settings/results/chains/M8_s0_D.npz); two-sided
metrics.xcpu_bits: code-bit agreement between two CPU fp32 runs on different machines / OS / BLAS, pooled over the compared residues (the F2c cross-machine threshold)

device_classes.gpu: CUDA, FoldMatch default (fp32 weights, bf16 autocast inside ESM3.logits); P0.5: 4 x A100-SXM4-40GB, torch 2.11.0+cu130 (enc_check also on an A100-PCIE-40GB: identical 576,399 / 580,608 bits)
device_classes.cpu: fp32 CPU; P0.5: AMD EPYC 7763 Linux (16 ranks x 8 threads, torch 2.11.0+cu130 CPU path, MKL) and Apple M1 Max macOS (7 threads, torch 2.11.0, Accelerate)
device_classes.mps: Apple MPS fp32 (D18); P0.5: M1 Max, torch 2.11.0
device_classes.mixed: query encodings from one device class, target codes from another (every ordered pair of the device classes A4 runs)

gates.reason: (1) The provisional CPU value assumed CPU fp32 would sit further from the research bf16 codes than the GPU path; P0.5 shows the opposite (CPU/MPS 0.99561, GPU 0.99511 pooled over 50.2M bits). (2) At the provisional values the gate could not bind before the dlnE gate: dlnE on P_sub is driven by target-code flips (research q x device codes: median 0.048-0.049, P95 0.152-0.165; device q x research codes: median 0.009-0.010, P95 0.038-0.039), and its P95 grows roughly in proportion to the bit disagreement, so the dlnE P95 bound 0.5 (~3x observed) corresponds to ~1.4% disagreement; 0.990 (1.0%, 2.0-2.3x observed) keeps the two gates consistent. (3) Every P0.5 set clears it: the lowest are the 50,000 A5 targets on GPU (25,000 of them reversed decoys; 0.99273 over 1.02e9 bits) and the 50-item enc_check (GPU 0.99275, CPU 0.99334). The residual disagreement is mainly FoldMatch path vs research path (bf16-weight, batched SequenceOnlyESM3): FoldMatch GPU vs FoldMatch CPU agree to 0.99739 and CPU Mac vs CPU Linux to 0.99997.

Observed over all 16 device x device configs on P_sub (831 pairs): median 0.049-0.051, P95 0.159-0.170, P99 <= 0.245, max <= 0.387, i.e. 2x (median) and ~3x (P95) margin. The shipped table's own split-vs-all stability is max |dlnE| 0.47 at E = 1 (ship_final.json), so a P95 of 0.5 stays inside the calibration uncertainty; nothing in P0.5 argues for loosening, and tightening would only shrink the margin against GPU-model / library drift without catching a failure the A4-bits gate would miss.

Observed |dF1| <= 0.00088 over 14 FoldMatch-path configs (pair-bootstrap 95% CIs within [-0.0023, +0.0022]); the research chain-set differences between SW settings it treated as material were >= 0.03 (B/C vs A), and setting D vs A was +0.005 (no cost). 0.01 has >10x margin and is not loosened; the provisional wording is read as two-sided because a shift of either sign beyond 0.01 would indicate a pipeline change, not ESM3 noise.

Observed CPU Mac (M1 Max, torch BLAS = Accelerate) vs CPU Linux (EPYC 7763, torch BLAS = MKL) 0.9999666 pooled over 50.2M bits (1,678 bits differ), worst item 0.99955 over 2,598 items; fp16 rows cosine >= 0.99999989 (rel. Frobenius 2.4e-5); MPS vs either CPU 0.99997. 0.995 would accept 150x the observed cross-machine disagreement (e.g. a CPU path with reduced-precision matmuls); 0.999 is 30x the pooled and 2.2x the worst per-item disagreement, so a correct fp32 CPU run on another machine is not expected to fail it on a pooled fixture (F2c).

invariants: every embedding finite; max |per_residue_embedding| < 65,504 (P0.5 max 16,795 on the A5 targets)
0 <unk> tokens and token count = L + 2 for every P0.5 input (498 A5 targets carry X/U/B)
a Q90 / lnE computed from research encodings reproduces bench_q90_shipped.npy and the research S_D matrices (P0.5: identical Q90; P_sub S max |d| 1e-4)
on_failure: Stop and report (plan G8). The remedy is the v2 refit (plan P0.5): re-encode the panel and the benchmark with FoldMatch, rerun ship.py / fit_final2.py unchanged, ship esm-codes-v2; v1 artefacts are never edited. A threshold is never relaxed to make A4 pass.
D18: MPS meets every CPU gate in P0.5 (bits 0.99561, dlnE median 0.051 / P95 0.159, dF1 +0.0004; MPS vs CPU 0.99997) -> allow MPS. Condition: release the MPS allocator cache per protein (torch.mps.empty_cache); without it one process's footprint reached 83 GB after ~800 variable-length proteins (tsub + panel) on a 64 GB M1 Max, the machine swapped and throughput fell to ~40 res/s; with the per-protein release the driver memory stayed at 6.1-6.5 GiB and throughput was 700-900 res/s (Mac CPU fp32: 170-210). Mixed GPU/CPU/MPS use passes every mixed gate.
